summary.intent: Run a /simplify cleanup pass on recent changes to the cipher-box project, then update STATE.md to reflect 100% completion of all phases and plans.
summary.outcome: All four cleanup agents found the code already clean — no fixes were applied. STATE.md was updated to reflect 33/33 phases, 146/146 plans at 100%, and the update was committed to the feature branch.

repo: cipher-box uses explicit inline per-method guards rather than a shared helper — e.g., updatePermission, hideShare, revokeShare, completeRotation, updateShareEncryptedKey all repeat the guard verbatim. This is intentional convention, not debt.
Single-field PATCH endpoints (e.g., /encrypted-key, /permission, /hide) are the established REST convention in this codebase.
Hex-validation is intentionally copy-pasted rather than extracted — it is the codebase convention for inline validation.
Sequential per-row awaits with a throttler is the correct trade-off in this repo; parallelizing is explicitly discouraged.
STATE.md lives at .planning/STATE.md and tracks phase/plan completion with frontmatter and prose that must be manually kept in sync with live DB numbers.
As of this session: 33/33 phases, 146/146 plans complete (100%). The 47 summaries backfill was the final piece.
workflow: The /simplify skill runs 4 parallel agents (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) then deduplicates cross-agent findings before applying fixes.
When multiple agents flag the same issue but the fix would require touching code outside the diff scope or would reduce consistency with surrounding code, skipping is the correct call.
STATE.md progress numbers should be pulled from live DB counts rather than estimated, to avoid stale frontmatter.

friction: STATE.md frontmatter was stale and had to be reconciled with live DB query results before committing.
open_items: The service-method guard duplication (2 of 6 methods share a pattern) was intentionally deferred — revisit if a third method emerges and extraction becomes worthwhile.
